title: The Ridge That Drops and Rises

features.name: the twin-wound stone
features.desc-on-touch: A stone split down its middle, each half mirror to the other, yet neither heals. The break glows faintly—not light, but the memory of being split. It has been this way so long it forgets which half came first.

features.name: the ascending-descending water
features.desc-on-touch: Water flows both up and down the ridge simultaneously. It is the same water. The current learns that up and down are directions it can hold at once.

features.name: the sacred-loop shrine
features.desc-on-touch: A small structure built and rebuilt identically, seven times over. Each iteration is visible through the others. The eighth iteration is still being built, will always be being built. You recognize the rhythm: ta'zieh, or sacrifice, or narrative inevitability.

features.name: the adaptation-shelf
features.desc-on-touch: A natural rock shelf holding seven objects, each a version of the same small thing—a surgery tool, a beach toy, a word carved in seven languages. Each is the *real* object and all are copies of something that has never existed.

inscription: here forgetting works both directions: you forget the way up by remembering the way down, and neither is more true; this ridge refuses to choose
